articles.body:
Want the upper hand over your opponents in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 ? Fortunately, we're here to help. After spending many years with Call of Duty's multiplayer, we've managed to compile a list of all the best Controller and Graphics settings to help give you the advantage over other players in MW4.

So whether it's adjusting your sensitivity, turning off common controller effects, prioritizing reload and tactical sprint, or even adjusting your graphics, we've got you covered with the best settings to use Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 .

If you're jumping into the MW4, adjusting your graphics settings can not only boost your FPS and general performance on PC, but it can also give you a slight competitive edge over other players if you tweak them just right.

While many of the graphics settings are dependent on your personal preference and PC specifications, there are few select settings that can make a real difference towards visibility and performance, namely those that fall under Post Processing Effects, Shadow and Lighting, and View.

Below is a list of all our recommended graphics settings for Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, based on our experience in-game so far.

Best Controller Settings for MW4 (PlayStation and Xbox Controller Settings)

Below is a list of the best controller settings for Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4. These recommended adjustments help maximize your effectiveness in combat and improve your overall experience by fine-tuning and adjusting settings that would otherwise put you at a disadvantage.

articles.title: DMZ Beginner’s Guide: 12 Things You Need to Know - Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Guide - IGN
articles.summary: DMZ is back in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, with major upgrades over the previous installment from Modern Warfare 2. Before you land in Hajin,
articles.body:
DMZ is back in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 , with major upgrades over the previous installment from Modern Warfare 2. Before you land in Hajin, there’s plenty you’ll need to be equipped for, whether that's completing side quests or taking down Lieutenants. This DMZ guide covers everything you need to know about this returning mode, from understanding the 3D Printer to uncovering hidden caches and recipes, rescuing your Operator, and extracting when you’re ready.

DMZ Beginner’s Guide: 12 Things You Need to Know

When you first enter DMZ, you’ll begin in the Forward Operating Base, or otherwise known as the FOB. Here, you can hang out with your squad, manage your stash, equip gear, buy new weapons, hunt bosses or other players, view orders, and ultimately prepare for your next deployment.

Before you deploy though, make sure you head over to your stash to equip your loadout. Once you're in the stash menu, you can equip a Weapon, a Backpack, an Armor Vest, a Medkit, Self-Revive, and other useful items you may need in deployment. What you select is what you’ll be bringing in, so make sure you pack accordingly.

If you don’t have enough gear to fill your pack, or if you've had some unfortunate luck in previous deployments, you can always opt for freebies by toggling the Equip Free Loadout option in the Ready Up menu. When toggled on, you will be supplied with random guns, equipment, and meds before your deployment.

When you’re ready to go, head over and interact with the barbed wire near the helicopter to deploy. Next, you're going to pick your deployment type.

When deploying, you’ll be presented with three different options. The first option is Story Missions , which are essentially the DMZ Orders. These story missions are designed to help you learn the ropes of DMZ and complete various activities around the map. Selecting this option not only matches you with other players working on story missions, but also rewards you with equipment recipes, Fire Support, Cash, and other helpful items. Keep in mind that while these missions are more tutorial-based, they gradually get harder as you work through them.

The next game mode option is Dynamic Operations . This will give you an immediate task to work toward when you infill. Each completed Dynamic Op rewards you with a Supply Drop of increasing rarity, plus 10,000 to 20,000 Cash . If you’d prefer more freedom to explore, choose Free Roam , which, as the name implies, means you’ll be deployed without any missions and can explore without constraints.

Once you deploy in DMZ, you'll be able to loot, complete side quests, and fight both AI and other online players. You'll have 30 minutes to get in and get out before the radiation starts spreading.

As you explore the map of Hajin, you’ll find loot all over, especially in buildings, cabinets, shelves, PCs, and duffle bags. Occasionally, you’ll even find loot on tables.

Items like Synthetics and Chemicals will be sent automatically to your stash. Other items, however, will be color-coded by rarity, letting you choose whether to pick them up or leave them behind. You’ll even be able to find hidden caches that are partially buried around the map, which will occasionally contain helpful items like armor plates and more.

Other loot to keep an eye out for includes recipes and manuals . These items are crucial to succeeding in DMZ, since you can’t start crafting with your 3D printer until you exfil with the right recipe, or use guns from the Gunsmith until you have extracted with the related manual.

Keep Your Eyes Peeled for Gas Stations, Fire Stations, Clinics, and More

In a twist of realism, you’ll also want to keep your eyes peeled for certain buildings when exploring Hajin, as some contain unique loot that you’ll need for survival. For example, Gas Stations often have Gas Cans you can use to fill up your vehicle as you traverse the map.

Fire Stations , aptly colored red, often hold radiation-reducing items like Radiation Blockers or Gas Masks , which you’ll need if radiation hits before you can exfil.

Medical Clinics , colored light green, have medical items on hand, such as Med Kits and Bandages, which are highly recommended to have in your loadout before each deployment. These are particularly helpful because if you get knocked down, you can use a Med Kit to pick yourself back up, or temporarily restore some health with Bandages.

You’re not guaranteed to find a Med Kit, but Clinics do offer a higher chance of finding one. Alternatively, you can search individual houses, which occasionally have Medicine Cabinets you can raid.

Another key building type to keep an eye out for is the blue-colored Police Stations . Once you’ve cleared the station of all enemies, it’s time to begin the search for supplies. You’ll often stumble upon locked rooms with regular caches , weapon caches , field upgrades , tacticals , and equipment . The more you loot, the rarer the loot and recipes will become—this is what makes these locations so valuable. In some cases, you may need to solve a hidden puzzle to unlock them, or even find a Key somewhere around the building.

The Casino is another notable location for rare loot and tons of cash, but getting in safely won’t be easy, as the area will be crawling with enemies.

One important thing to note is that each area you visit has a threat level indicated in the middle of the screen , just beneath your compass . This level indicates how dangerous an area is. The higher the level, the more dangerous the enemy response will be in the area. Remember: the higher the threat, the more likely you are to be engaged in combat, which, as a result, means other players will also be alerted to your location.

As we’ve explained earlier, Recipes and Weapon Manuals aren’t easy to find and will require a lot of grinding to unlock them all. So, when you kill an AI enemy and find a weapon you’d like to use, you’ll probably want to pick it up. But before you do, be careful, because their gun could be broken, which could land you in risky waters, especially if you’re surrounded.

There are a few ways you can tell if a weapon is broken. The first is a small red square that appears below the weapon icon; the weapon’s magazine capacity might be smaller than normal; or its optic might be smashed.

Take on Missions and Boss Board Challenges

Another big aspect of the DMZ experience is the Dynamic Ops . When you deploy into this game mode, you’ll receive a randomized mission—they’re also available in Free Roam, but you’ll need to actively seek out the Phone/Contact icons around the map in order to start them.

Now, each Dynamic Ops mission will differ in both objectives and difficulty—some will have a ton of objectives to complete, while others will be on the simpler side. For example, one mission we encountered involved tracking down and hunting a high-value target, and another required us to defend and capture a site—all of which were against the AI enemies.

With that said though, if you’re looking for one of the tougher challenges in DMZ, outside other players, you can opt to visit the Boss Board at your Forward Operations Base, which will display a list of Lieutenants and Commanders. Here, you will have the opportunity to purchase intel about them (or complete missions for intel), as well as take on Kill Challenges and Dog Tag Challenges .

Some missions will have you do things like find and hunt a high-value target, plant a bomb to destroy supplies, or even defend and capture the same site. All of these will give you plenty of AI to fight.

If you’d prefer not to purchase intel, you can always look for Lieutenant Hunt towers for more precise intel. The only downside to this is that it will give you the location of a random Lieutenant, so it may not be the one you’re looking for.

Before you start fighting Lieutenants, make sure you’re prepared and geared accordingly. At a minimum, we recommend a strong weapon, a tier two vest, and a self-revive.

As you near a Lieutenant, you will see their hologram pop up. Each will be kitted out with different guns and equipment, and will require a different strategy to take them down. Again, Lieutenants are among the most challenging aspects of DMZ outside regular players, so we don’t recommend taking them lightly, as they will put up a good challenge.

Once you’ve managed to eliminate a Lieutenant, they will drop a Dog Tag . This is where things get tricky: picking up the tag marks this case on the tac map, making you a prime target for nearby players, so make sure you’re ready for surprise attacks.

Rather than just being the hunted though, you can in turn become the hunter and track down other players who are also tracking Lieutenants and have Dog Tags on them that you can loot from their pack, as their general area will be marked on the map. You really only have two options. Either prep for the PvP challenge that may come your way, or quickly exfil.

You’ll face upwards of 60 players in DMZ, all of whom are spread either across teams of up to four people, or even solo players. So, there’s a chance you could face max teams or a solo player—it really just depends on who’s in your lobby.

If you played the DMZ beta, one thing you may notice is that when your squad is eliminated, your operator will be missing in action. There is no ability to plead, and you will lose everything in your backpack.

When your operator is missing, you can rescue them, which reinstates the Traits Purchased, any Unspent Trait Points, and your Operator's Dog Tag Rank, but you'll lose most of the Operator’s loadout. In terms of cost, this will set you back quite a bit, but the total amount depends on how leveled up they are.

You can also opt to start a new Operator, however, there is one limitation, as you cannot select the same Operator. For example, if Park goes missing in action, you can’t create a new Operator using Park. You can change their skins, though.

If your squad survives before the radiation timer ends, you will need to get to an exfil location . These locations are conveniently marked on the map with an icon displaying a person leaving a door. The exfil point in-game will also feature green smoke that you’ll be able to spot from a distance. To call in the helicopter, simply interact with the smoke to call them in.

Plan accordingly, as when you view the map, you’ll notice a yellow radiation circle . The exfil closest to this circle will close first as it slowly expands across the map. Exfils can be used multiple times, so if another team happens to use it before you, simply wait for the cooldown period to end.

You can also complete the Dynamic Op , Sky Heist . Essentially, this allows you to pilot a helicopter. One person will need to fly, while the rest of the team fend off enemies. The added bonus to this Op is that it gives you your own private exfil. It’s not all easy flying though, as it can be a little challenging to defend the helicopter from being shot out of the sky by tailing enemy AI.

Once you successfully extract, you will get an extraction summary that details all the valuable items you’ve collected, printer ingredients you’ve stashed, cash banked, and other handy summaries. You will also receive a combat rating. This rating is based on completed objectives, how well you engaged in combat encounters, and your looting ability. We’ve found that our best ranks came from doing a little bit of everything, so keep that in mind on your next deployment.

The XP you earn from completing Ops, earning kills, and bonuses adds directly to your DMZ level, which caps at level 70—unlike your Multiplayer level, your DMZ level can only be leveled inside DMZ.

As you level up your operator, you’ll earn Trait Points . You can use these to purchase Operator Traits , which are essentially perks that can provide in-game advantages. There are three dedicated skills: Warfighter , Scout , and Survivalist .

Given DMZ's nature, we recommend creating different Operators based on your needs. For example, you might have one Operator focused mostly on combat, while another focuses on sleuthing and looting. However, as you pick the first trait, the next set is completely random, so you may get something different every single time.

As you level up your operator and unlock all 18 Trait Points, you can eventually prestige your operator and get three permanent traits. You can keep progressing with your operator, but based on our early experience, the rewards weren’t really worth it, and it will keep costing you more money each time.

As you return to the FOB, you'll want to manage your Stash. To get started, we recommend emptying everything you have collected from your backpack. As you empty it, keep an eye out for items you can sell . These are indicated by a diamond symbol on the item icon.

These items can be quite valuable, so selling them will put cash in the bank for rescuing your Operator, buying gunsmith attachments, purchasing guns from vendors, or unlocking new upgrades at your FOB. In addition to looking for valuable items, you’ll also want to look for items marked with a small square icon—this indicates a component needed for the 3D printer .

The 3D printer is a crucial machine in DMZ, as it lets you print upgrades, equipment, and other items you’ll use on all your deployments. When it comes to making your first upgrade, we highly recommend going with the first Bank Upgrade , which will set you back just $20,000 .

Then, when you can afford it, the second Bank Upgrade is also a very worthy purchase. The reason is that once you hit your bank limit, you can’t earn any more money until you either spend it or buy another upgrade. This can be very limiting, especially if you hit your cap unexpectedly and miss out on thousands of dollars.

The rest of the 3D printer upgrades will mostly depend on which recipes you've unlocked and which upgrades you want to do first, whether that’s the Stash Weapon Upgrade , Vendor Upgrade , or something else entirely. The more tasks and Ops you complete, the more cash you’ll have banked to buy better weapons or more space.

If you want a specific upgrade but are missing certain ingredients, you can track the recipes in the 3D Printer menu or even view where to find your missing ingredients.

articles.title: 'League of Legends: New Dawn': Riot anuncia aguardada reformulação do game para 2027 | G1
articles.standfirst: Desenvolvedora apresentou título e teaser do aguardado projeto de renovação do moba, mas sem muitos detalhes. Mais informações serão divulgadas em janeiro.
articles.summary: Desenvolvedora apresentou título e teaser do aguardado projeto de renovação do moba, mas sem muitos detalhes. Mais informações serão divulgadas em janeiro.
articles.body:
"League of Legends: New Dawn" será o nome da aguardada reformulação do moba da Riot, prometida para 2027. O anúncio foi feito pela desenvolvedora neste sábado (14), durante a final do seu mundial, realizado em Nova York, Estados Unidos.

O projeto, trabalhado internamente como "League Next", deve renovar o programa de integração dos jogos da empresa (chamado de client).

O teaser revelado neste sábado também indica mudanças nos visuais dos campeões e alterações nos caminhos do mapa principal.

Animação 'A new dawn', de 'League of Legends', em 2014 — Foto: Reprodução/YouTube/League of Legends

Apesar de ser chamado pelos fãs de "League of Legends 2", o agora batizado de "New Dawn" não é uma continuação em si, nem um jogo separado do original, mas um pacote de reformulações que busca atrair novos jogadores para o game de competição online, um dos mais populares do mundo.

A apresentação não relevou grandes detalhes, mas a Riot promete mais informações em janeiro.

articles.title: Cooking Guide - WoW Forever Guide - IGN
articles.summary: World of Warcraft: Forever features an abundant variety of Professions, which are special skills that players can level separately and use to gather and craft
articles.body:
World of Warcraft: Forever features an abundant variety of Professions, which are special skills that players can level separately and use to gather and craft items to bolster their characters in one way or another. Investing in both primary and secondary professions is a must if you want to make the most of your journey through Azeroth, so knowing which ones to pursue and how they work is one of the first things you want to learn.

Below is our comprehensive World of Warcraft: Forever Cooking Guide, detailing how to unlock it, the tools you need to make use of it, and the best dishes to craft.

Cooking is one of the game's Secondary Professions (e.g. - First Aid, Fishing), which are professions that are more universal in their utility and can be freely unlocked without sacrificing one of the two slots that are allocated for Primary Professions (e.g. - Blacksmithing, Leatherworking, Alchemy).

This means that all players, regardless of their character's class and faction, should unlock and level up Cooking as much as possible , given the benefits it can provide in terms of buffs to your given class and even other professions. Or, if you're someone who simply wants to make as much gold as possible, then cooking the most lucrative dishes to sell via the Auction House can provide a good stream of money that you can put towards the game's pricier investments, such as mount unlocks.

There's a total of four ranks to unlock while leveling the Cooking profession. Each one requires reaching a certain skill point threshold, and the final two ranks require a couple of additional steps.

To unlock Cooking, you'll first need to visit one of the game's many Cooking Trainers scattered around Azeroth. Each Profession has its own type of respective trainer that's responsible for helping you rank up and providing the means you need to maximize that profession's capabilities.

Whether you're Alliance or Horde, there are several available within capital cities and other hubs across different zones. These NPCs are where you'll unlock at least the first two ranks of Cooking and some of them also carry recipes and ingredients.

Once you've found one of these Trainers, pick the 'Apprentice' training option and pay the required fee to officially unlock Cooking.

Each faction has several Cooking Trainers located across their respective aligned regions. You can visit any of these Trainers to get access to the first two ranks of Cooking, while the latter two ranks require special steps to unlock.

There's a total of 10 Cooking Trainers found in Alliance regions. Below is a list of all their designated locations.

There's a total of 11 Cooking Trainers found in Horde regions. Below is a list of all their designated locations.

To cook anything, you need to have a campfire lit and ready first. Granted, that's not something you always need to supply yourself, as campfires are traditionally found near Cooking trainers to give you easy access for all your cooking needs. Also, you can often find campfires placed by other players in or near major hubs.

Otherwise, to make your own campfire, you need to make use of Basic Campfire Kits , and the recipe for that automatically becomes available when you first unlock Cooking. Crafting them requires Simple Wood along with Flint and Tinder , and you can then tuck them away in your inventory for whenever you need to set up camp. There are also Journeyman and Expert Campfire Kits you can unlock with enough Cooking Skill Points (90 and 200 respectively) and the respective blueprints (Journeyman Campfire and Expert Campfire).

Once you have a campfire in place, open your Cooking menu and select a dish you want to cook from the recipes you've already unlocked. You can't cook a dish if you don't have the recipe for it yet. Your available recipes are further subdivided based on their utility. At the top is 'Everyday Meals' and beneath that are foods categorized by stat type (e.g. - Stamina, Strength, Agility, Intellect). So if you need something to boost your Agility stat, for instance, then cook a dish from that submenu.

Cooking is a profession that requires a good amount of patience to level and knowing how to keep your costs as minimal as possible while doing so.

The biggest key to this is to level Fishing in tandem with your Cooking profession , as fishing can provide you with the primary ingredients for recipes that are the most efficient at giving you skill points. This way you minimize having to run around to purchase ingredients from vendors or the Auction House and keep your costs low, ideally to just purchasing recipes.

Once you've unlocked the Apprentice Cooking rank, focus your first 50 skill points on cooking either Brilliant Smallfish and/or Slitherskin Mackerel . The recipes for these are available from vendors in every starting area for both factions.

Alternatively, you can also cook either Charred Wolf Meat or Roasted Boar Meat using Stringy Wolf Meat or Chunks of Boar Meat (respectively) from creatures you slay. The recipes for those are provided by Cooking Trainers.

When you hit 50 Cooking skill points, visit your Trainer to unlock the Journeyman Cooking rank. From this point, you'll want to focus on cooking either Longjaw Mud Snapper or Rainbow Fin Albacore , and the recipes for those are also available from vendors in several different major locales for both factions.

Alternatively, you can also opt to cook Smoked Bear Meat via any Bear Meat you collect during your quest grind. That recipe is available from either Andrew Hilbert (Horde) in Silverpine Forest or Drac Roughcut (Alliance) in Loch Modan .

Another good option is Strider Stew , which you can cook using Strider Meat from killed mobs and Shiny Red Apples. Depending on your starting area, those apples can be collected in tandem with early-game quests, letting you bypass the cost of buying them from vendors. The recipe for this dish is provided by Tari'qa in The Barrens or as a reward from the Easy Strider Living quest (Alliance only) .

Once you hit the 100 skill point mark, you can and should integrate either the Bristle Whisker Catfish or Cooked Crab Claw recipe into your cooking routine. Just note that while the recipe for Bristle Whisker Catfish can be purchased from NPCs in several areas for both factions, the Cooked Crab Claw recipe can only be purchased from Kendor Kabonka in Stormwind City, which locks it to Alliance players.

Once you reach at least 125 Cooking skill points, it's time to unlock your Expert Cooking rank. To do that, you need to get your hands on the Expert Cookbook, which is sold by one of two vendors, depending on your character's given faction.

Alliance - Sold by Shandrina in Ashenvale at Mystral Lake (49.6, 67.0)

Horde - Sold by Wulan in Desolace at Shadowprey Village (26.2, 69.8)

Once you have the book, use it to unlock your Expert Cooking rank, at which point you can continue leveling.

At this point, Bristle Whisker Catfish remains a viable option to craft until about 150 skill points. From there, you should pivot to other recipes including the Curiously Tasty Omelet , which can be purchased either from Keena (Horde) in the Arathi Highlands or from Kendor Kabonka (Alliance) in Stormwind City. Meanwhile, there's also Goblin Deviled Clams , which can be purchased from Cooking Trainers, and Hot Lion Chops which is available from Zargh (Horde) in The Barrens.

At the 175 skill point mark, you can integrate the Roast Raptor recipe , which can be purchased from either Keena (Horde) in the Arathi Highlands, Ogg'marr (Horde) in Dustwallow Marsh, or from Hammon Karwn (Alliance) who's also in the Arathi Highlands. Another good option is the Mithril Headed Trout recipe, which is a widely available one from vendors in most major hubs/cities.

At 225 Cooking skill points, you can unlock the fourth and final rank of your profession, but this time you'll need to complete a quest to do so. The quest is Clamlette Surprise found in Tanaris at Gadgetzan , and you must have both 225 Cooking and have your character at Level 35 to obtain it. The quest NPC is Dirge Quikcleave , the local butcher.

However, before you get that quest, you'll need to complete a pre-requisite one that hinges on your faction.

Alliance - I Know A Guy - Daryl Riknussun in Ironforge

Horde - To Gadgetzan You Go! - Zamja in Orgrimmar

Also, while you're doing your designated quest for this, take the time to gather 12 x Giant Egg , 10 x Zesty Clam Meat , and 20 x Alterac Swiss , as you'll need them for Clamette Surprise once you unlock it. Otherwise you can wait and do the gathering at that point, but it's to save you some travel time.

Either way, once you turn in the aforementioned items to Dirge, he'll provide you with Artisan Cooking as your main reward.

Beyond this point, to reach your final goal of 300 Cooking skill points, your two best bets in terms of recipes are Spotted Yellowtail and Filet of Redgill. The Spotted Yellowtail recipe can be purchased from Gikkix at Stormwheedle Port in Tanaris (Poached Sunscale Salmon is a good alternative sold by them as well). Meanwhile, the Filet of Redgill recipe is available from Kelsey Vance in Stranglethorn Vale.

articles.title: GTA 6 Leak Seemingly Reveals Official Album's Full Track List Days Before Launch
articles.summary: The full track list for Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album seems to have leaked online just days before GTA 6's launch.
articles.body:
The full track list for Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album seems to have leaked online just days before GTA 6 's launch.

Rockstar Games just can't catch a break. After weeks of unprecedented leaks were published online, even more information about GTA 6 has found its way onto the internet, this time revealing the entire list of every song and artist featured on the official soundtrack's album release.

As 13 years turns into just a few days, more leaks felt inevitable. The latest breach arrived in the form of a video shared on social media from what appears to be a Barnes & Noble-like retailer. The main clip being passed around is still up hours later and shows the front, back, and spines of the Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album's double LP vinyl. As you might have guessed, the $50 soundtrack isn't planned to hit store shelves until November 19, 2026.

Although there are likely even more tunes tucked into the game itself, an early glimpse at the GTA 6 soundtrack means we now know every song and artist featured on its official album. Rolling Stone has confirmed the track list with its sources. We won't beat around the bush; you can see the full Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album track list below.

Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album Leaked Track List

Starting from Zero – Justice (feat. Michael McDonald)

That's It – Yung Lean (feat. Future & Metro Boomin)

Sexy Magic – CA7RIEL & Paco Amoroso, PinkPantheress, Fred Again.. & Étienne de Crécy

We've gotten tastes of the music Rockstar hand-selected to be featured through the years, with stars like Travis Scott, Future, and Morgan Wallen teasing their inclusion as recently as September . We also got to hear some of GTA 6's tunes with the premiere of the Extended Look back in August. As many guessed, the developers have given players a solid playlist of songs from a variety of genres to jam to as they speed through Vice City.

Fans will note this is different from the Grand Theft Auto VI: Original Score by Grammy Award-winning French electronic duo Justice. It's also set to get its own release for physical music collectors, with its release date set for December 11, 2026.

GTA 6, of course, will launch for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X | S November 19, 2026. Today, we also learned that Rockstar has promised next week's new game will include mechanisms to encourage empathy for the first time in the franchise's history . Yesterday, Rockstar revealed a closer look at an animated TV series called Macca & Friends that can be watched in-game.

For more, you can check out IGN's collection of GTA 6's songs and radio stations . You can also check out how some recent gameplay clips are blowing players (and IGN ) away.

Michael Cripe is a freelance writer with IGN. He's best known for his work at sites like The Pitch, The Escapist, and OnlySP. Be sure to give him a follow on Bluesky (@mikecripe.bsky.social) and Twitter (@MikeCripe).

articles.title: Notre-Dame - Finding the Brittle King Walkthrough - Castlevania: Belmont's Curse Guide - IGN
articles.summary: This is a continuation of IGN's walkthrough for Castlevania: Belmont's Curse. Here, we'll be focusing on the Brittle King, one of the optional
articles.body:
This is a continuation of IGN's walkthrough for Castlevania: Belmont's Curse . Here, we'll be focusing on the Brittle King, one of the optional bosses that you can find while exploring Notre-Dame . The Brittle King is among the optional routes you can chase after as Rose, after you defeat the Shadow , revealed as Death. You'll unlock your double jump, allowing you to explore multiple locations that you previously couldn't reach. You can follow along with this playthrough to review the previous sections here .

Although the Brittle King is one of the Tarot cards that you can see in your deck, finding him requires you to directly seek him. You'll be able to do this after defeating the Shadow . You want to remain in Notre-Dame for this part as well. After you leave the room where Rose spoke with Trevor and received the Vampire Killer whip, make your way to the Mirror of Life in West Triforium. It's a route you had to go through when you wanted to reach the La Fleche, which we'll be going through on our way to unlocking the Brittle King.

From the West Triforium, we'll be making our way to the right and dashing across to the La Fleche. As you've already defeated the Shadow and unlocked all of the melodies, this route should be familiar to you. Inside the La Fleche, take the right path, rather than going down or up. This brings you to the East Triforium.

Head down from the starting platform at the East Triforium, where you'll find four different beams shooting down from the top area. There's a skeleton archer and a gargoyle between the first and second beams.

Rather than going directly down the middle, you can use the gargoyle as a leaping point to take you over the top section, bypassing the two middle ones, and take you to the other side. There's still the final beam (with another gargoyle and skeleton), but it's a viable path forward to reach the other side.

On this side, there's an armored knight with a large shield blocking your path, and a breakable floor piece. The way you find the Brittle King is through the breakable floor piece, but you won't have enough space to smash down unless you get higher. For now, take out the shield knight, and then head to the right side of this area. Stop at the glowing door, and there's a purple anchor above you. This can help you get enough height to break through the floor, but you have to complete this tricky puzzle.

You want to take the purple anchor up, and then latch on to the wall. Carefully, you want to slide down enough so that you have enough space to jump and then dash to the left, through the gap between the spikes, and land on the breakable platform. You need to time reaching the purple anchor and sliding onto the wall so that you land on the breakable platform while the beam in the middle is down. You can then perform a standard jump to the next breakable platform on the left side of it.

Here's the tough part. From the second breakable platform on the left side, jump up and dash through the glowing abyss shards. You need to have your Halo activated to do this. Once you're through the shards, turn off the Halo and latch onto the abyss shards on the wall. Hold it here for a second, then perform a jump off the shards to your left, and then perform a Talos Fist smash downward, landing on the floor piece below you.

You should be able to bypass the pair of beams below you and break through the floor, taking you to the East Gallery. You can break the door open to your left and continue your path.

In this next area, you'll have a single beam shooting horizontally across the entire room. There's a yellow anchor above you. When the beam is not shooting, jump and swing to the left. You want to try to stretch this swing out as far as you can before you need to take a jump (potentially a second one), and then a dash.

Your goal is to reach the second yellow anchor on this side and swing as far as you can to the left. Below you (and between several spikes) is a breakable floor piece.

When you're above it, smash down, and you should break through it. Immediately in this section is an enemy ambush room, and you'll need to fight through the waves of skeletons with boomerangs, knights, and a large golem that appears during the final wave to proceed forward.

In the next room, there's a criss-cross section of beams in the center of the room. Two of them are shooting upward, and the other are shooting down the middle. You have a pair of yellow anchors on the left side. You want to take the first one to swing you to the right, and then use the second one to gain momentum through the center of the room. Your goal is to swing across and move through the two upward-shooting beams, using a dash and a double-jump to cross the spikes on the right side.

If you have the time, try to time your swing on the second anchor to get to the middle of the room (above the pair of beams shooting horizontally), and then smash down. There's a breakable floor section that you can access, revealing a Relic chest. You'll unlock the Eldritch Talisman (Rose is invulnerable for 15 seconds after resting in a save room. The duration of invulnerability after taking damage is also doubled). After getting down, continue your path to the upper section, and land on the right side of the spikes.

You'll reach a blocked door on the right side that you can break through and take the purple anchor to the upper section, unlocking the East Gallery's Mirror of Life. It's an ideal checkpoint for the Brittle King.

After getting this Mirror of Life, return to the East Gallery and break through the door to the left of this room. It reconnects you to the start of the East Gallery, allowing you to leave, but you want to head back down to where you came from.

Here, you'll find a boss room entrance, giving you access to the Brittle King.

When you enter the Brittle King's boss room, head to the center. There's a sword in the stone that you can interact with under multiple glass windows, reflecting the history and lore surrounding King Arthur.

Interact with the sword, and you'll unlock the only clue for the Brittle King, known as the Feat of Strength.

To interact with this sword, you need to make sure you have the Fist of Talos Arcana equipped on Rose. When you do, interact with the sword again, and you can attempt to remove it from the stone.

When Rose attempts to do this, the Brittle King begins to speak to Rose, saying that she needs more than mere strength to pull the sword from the stone. The stained glass shatters behind the sword, creating a large figure before Rose, revealing the Brittle King.

When the boss battle against the Brittle King begins, he's a slow-moving figure who gradually moves toward you throughout this fight. He primarily wants to keep his shield between you and him, as any attack you do in front of him is blocked by the shield, preventing him from taking any damage. Each time you hit the shield, chips break off and fly into the air. They hover in the air for a moment before locking onto your location and diving straight at you.

Expect these to appear throughout this encounter whenever you try hitting him. You need to aim above or below the shield to prevent this from happening. You won't have this happen if you're hitting the Brittle King from behind, but he's quick to pivot so he's facing you if you switch sides.

Notably, if you get too far away from the Brittle King, he'll hit his sword on his shield, causing chips to fly up into the air. As you might expect, they fly directly at you when this happens. The best way to dodge these chips is to wait until they're on the move, and slide or jump out of the way. They don't change direction when they're moving, only when they're preparing to fire.

Another attack the Brittle King will use against you is that if you're facing his front, he'll stab his sword above or below him. His shield will adjust to the opposite side of where he's stabbing. For example, if he's stabbing above, his shield goes down, preventing you from hitting his legs. You'll have to try to get him at his head, or wait until he's done attacking. Additionally, the sword stab goes out much farther than you might expect. You want to try jumping above it or ducking below it, based on which section the Brittle King is aiming at.

Finally, another attack that you can expect from the Brittle King is a jump. He'll be across the room from you and jump into the air. When he does this and lands, he'll smash down on the side he's jumping toward, sending glass flying into the air. Those glass shards will hover and rotate for a few seconds before homing in and locking on to you. There are several more glass shards in this attack than in previous ones, so expect to dodge multiple times.

When you get the Brittle King between 80 and 70% of his health, he'll go to the center of the room. He then screams, "Is it lasers? It is! It's lasers!" The beam of light that's shining out behind the broken glass window shines directly onto the shield the Brittle King is holding above him, and multiple lines go out underneath the shield.

The formations vary from single lines that spread from the shield before exploding, causing a larger area-of-effect around them (similar to the Shadows), but you can find safety by standing still. These gradually rotate, forcing you to change positions every time. Alternatively, you might get multiple lines that are clustered together, leaving large gaps for you to stand, but expect these to also move after they fire out, forcing you to change positions.

During this time, you can continue to attack Arthur while he does this. However, this may prove challenging give the frequency of the attacks and how much damage they do. I recommend lashing out with your weapon, or your Arcana, during these shield bursts to do the most damage. If you have an Arcana or weapon that has a damage-over-time effect, hitting Arthur once and then dodging the lasers might be a good strategy.

When the Brittle King stops this attack, he'll return to his usual attacks against you. However, if you were able to get him down below 50% while he was firing his lasers, he may pivot back into those again and force you to continue dodging. The lasers do reappear again as an attack when you get him down to the 30% to 20% health range, as well.

Beyond the lasers, Arthur doesn't change up too much of his attack pattern. When you get him down to zero, you'll be able to absorb him into your Tarot cards, unlocking his Arcana, the Stained-Glass Shield.

It's a spell that creates a magical shield around Rose, absorbing attacks. Rose takes no damage, interruptions, or special effects associated with the attack, and shards of glass fly towards enemies with this spell.

You also receive Arthur's sword, Excalibur, a legendary Greatsword that you can use.

With Arthur eliminated and absorbed into Rose's Tarot deck, he regains part of his sanity. Both Rose and Leon question how long Arthur has been under Dracula's control.

Although he cannot remember, he wishes to pledge himself to Rose's fight against Dracula and vows to assist in bringing him down.

The Brittle King was the final boss that you could fight in this location. With his defeat, you can make your way out of Notre-Dame and return to the Main Hall. You can choose to head there by going through the Notre-Dame painting entrance where you started, or you can use the Ferryman's Wharf and return to the Main Hall that way. Both methods are valid, but I'll use the painting entrance and return to the Main Hall through there.

When you arrive at the Main Hall, the next step will be to find additional hidden bosses. The next opponent we'll be focusing on is the Miser, who is hiding somewhere outside of Dracula's castle, and to do that, we're going to need to track down specific items to unlock his entrance. We'll be continuing that in the next section of our walkthrough.

articles.title: Where to Use the Field Depot Key - Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Found the Field Depot Key in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4's DMZ, but you're not sure where to find the room it unlocks? Here's exactly where
articles.body:
Found the Field Depot Key in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 's DMZ, but you're not sure where to find the room it unlocks? Here's exactly where you can find the Field Depot in DMZ .

You can find the Field Depot room inside the northeast building of the Chang-San Air Base , on Grid 5B , not too far from the main gate entrance. It's on the ground floor, and is found inside a smaller room, separate from the main larger warehouse. It can be quickly accessed from the main road side of the building, but beware of the soldiers guarding the area.

Up Next: Where to Use the Coin Mining Den Key

articles.summary: Found the Coin Mining Den Key in DMZ but you're not too sure where to use it? Here's exactly where you can find the Coin Mining Den in Call of Duty:
articles.body:
Found the Coin Mining Den Key in DMZ but you're not too sure where to use it? Here's exactly where you can find the Coin Mining Den in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 .

The Coin Mining Den is on the top floor of a small building in the southwest portion of Nurigo Mall , before you reach The Grid area, on grid tile G6 . When entering the building, simply use the stairs to reach the third floor, where you'll find the Coin Mining Den directly to your right when reaching the top. The room is marked by a blue 'Office' sign on the wall.

Found the Prison Encampment Storage Key in DMZ but you're not too sure where to use it? Here's exactly where you can find Prison Encampment Storage in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 .

The Prison Encampment Storage is on the east side of the 14th Political Prison , outside of the larger structure, close to the road on the west side of C3 . Head to the southern side of the building, where you'll find the large wooden, Prison Encampment Storage door.

articles.title: Where to Use the Militia Arms Depot Key - Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Got your hands on the Militia Arms Depot key in DMZ but you're not too sure where to find it? Here's exactly where you can find the Militia Arms
articles.body:
Got your hands on the Militia Arms Depot key in DMZ but you're not too sure where to find it? Here's exactly where you can find the Militia Arms Depot door in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 .

You can find the Militia Arms Depot between tiles G7 and G8 . Make your way to the base; you'll find the door on the first floor of the large blue building , which requires the Gangbyeon Apartment B Key . When reaching the first floor, you'll find the Militia Arms Depot door to your left.

You can find the Gangbyeon Apartment B between tiles G7 and G8 on the south of Compound Echo . You can enter the building from the ground floor if you have the key or you can take an alternate route that sees you entering through a window on the rear side (roadside) of the building.

To reach the window, head to the back of the building and look for structure found nearby. Climb up onto the structure, and once on top, run and jump across to the copper pipes found on the back of the building. Traverse these pipes and ledges until you reach the large window found near the top. Break through the window, and then begin searching the floor for the Gangbyeon Apartment B key - this key doesn't have a static spawn, so you may need to search several rooms until you find.

Up Next: Where to Use the Executive Arms Auction Key

articles.title: Meigu Lake Memory Flower Locations - Phantom Blade Zero Guide - IGN
articles.summary: There are 30 Memory Flower Petals in Meigu
articles.body:
There are 30 Memory Flower Petals in Meigu Lake.

From the docks, simply navigate northeast, southwest of the Meigu Songhouse Dock bell. You’ll see this first petal on the water, around some flowers.

This is Yan’er’s Memory Flower I - Allure of Vanity.

Southwest of the previous flower, you’ll see a small dock where you can find a hurt NPC and some other collectibles. Around this location, on the side with more vegetation, you’ll find this petal on the water.

This is Yan’er’s Memory Flower II - Bloodline.

Use your boat to go south of the Meigu Songhouse Dock area. On the water, in front of the big building and next to some rocks, you’ll see this petal.

This is Yan’er’s Memory Flower III - Into the Lake.

The next one is pretty close. Navigate east, without passing Meigu Sonhouse Dock, and you’ll find the flower next to a shipwreck.

This is Yan’er’s Memory Flower VI - All Has Changed.

In Meigu Village West Dock, after defeating the nearby enemies, enter the second building on the right. The flower is in a plant pot.

This is Blackwater Crew’s Memory Flower I - Fishing.

In Blackwater Crew Dock (northeast of Meigu Village West Dock), as soon as you enter the island, you’ll find a bell. To the left of the bell, climb the platform, deal with two fish fiends, and enter the building on the right. Here’s your petal.

This is Blackwater Crew’s Memory Flower III - Voluntary Transcension.
